article.Citation/Title: P.L. Prior, & Prior, S. L. (2014). Ibogaine effect on cocaine craving and use in dependent patients - a double-blind, placebo-controlled pilot study. Journal of Addiction and Therapy, 1(2), 1-4.
article.Outcome: Lower positive-urine (relapse) rate in the ibogaine group (corresponding to ~10% of the sample) vs the placebo group across the 24-week follow-up
article.InterventionDescription: Single 1800 mg oral encapsulated ibogaine (75% purity Tabernanthe iboga extract) vs placebo sugar-powder capsule; 72-hour inpatient cardiac monitoring, then biweekly outpatient follow-up to 24 weeks.

ae_events.Description: Visual hallucinations (small animals/vermin, weather changes, natural elements, shadows/apparitions) in ibogaine group during the 72h post-dose period, mainly in the first 24h

article.Outcome: Primary outcome is explicitly designated by the authors: 'the reduction in percentage of positive urine samples was considered the primary outcome' (Methods). The only reported statistic for this outcome describes a lower positive-urine (relapse) rate in the ibogaine group, 'corresponding to 10% of the sample,' vs a higher, unquantified rate in placebo (Results/Discussion, urine-sample paragraph). No paired absolute percentages for both arms are given, so Outcome is coded as a labelled descriptor rather than a number.
article.SD: Test statistic paired with the urine-positivity primary outcome, taken from the same sentence: 'F=2,450; df=3,12; p=0,023; ANOVA repeated measures.' Numerator df=3 is unusual for what otherwise reads as a 2-group comparison; the article never explains the 3 numerator df. This is flagged as an internal-consistency oddity rather than resolved or reinterpreted, per the no-decoding-theory rule.
article.PVal: p=0,023, reported directly alongside the F statistic for the urine-positivity primary outcome (same sentence as SD).
article.SampleSize_NFinal: N=20 (10 ibogaine, 10 placebo) enrolled. The Results open with 'There were no defects from either group during the 6 month evaluation period,' read here as no dropouts/attrition given its context alongside baseline-comparability reporting; no participant losses are described anywhere else, and the urine analysis is stated as using 'the total samples collected from the 24 week period.' 'Defects' is an apparent OCR/translation artifact (the authors are Brazilian); 'dropouts' is the most contextually consistent reading, but this is not fully unambiguous and is flagged per the non-fabrication rule.

MethodologyDescribedYN.note: No a priori/post hoc power calculation or sample-size justification is given (N=20 not justified). The method of group allocation is never described as random anywhere in the article (only 'sorted' into groups; the word 'random/randomized' never appears in the study's own methods text, despite the double-blind, placebo-controlled framing). All other elements -- objective, design, setting, eligibility, intervention, comparator, outcomes, blinding, statistics, results, harms, funding -- are described. 12/14 met, below the 13-of-14 threshold, so MethodologyDescribedYN=0.

article.Condition: This article is filed under Condition='Opioid' in the request manifest and SourcePDF path ('opioids/...'), but the trial is entirely about cocaine dependence (DSM-IV cocaine dependence diagnosis, cocaine urine screening, Minnesota Cocaine Craving Scale); ibogaine for opioid use is never mentioned in the text. Condition is echoed as instructed; this mismatch is a corpus-labeling finding, not something corrected here. Eligibility criterion (b) is judged met because cocaine craving/use is itself a substance-use outcome, independent of the Opioid filing label.
article.RandomizationYN: Coded '.' -- the study is called 'double blind, placebo controlled' throughout, including the title, but the word 'random'/'randomized' never appears anywhere in the article body describing this study's own methods; participants are only described as 'sorted' into 2 groups. Because the study has two arms (the concept clearly applies) but the allocation method is never stated, this is not-reported rather than not-applicable, and is not treated as the single-arm/open-label '0' boundary case.
article.Retention (%): Coded 100, based on no reported attrition anywhere in the article (see SampleSize_NFinal rationale), with denominator N=20 (enrolled total, used because randomization is not confirmed). Flagged because it rests on interpreting the garbled 'no defects' phrase as 'no dropouts.'
article.BaseStatus: Coded '.' -- inclusion criteria require DSM-IV cocaine dependence with self-reported use at least weekly for one month, but no severity instrument or score (e.g., ASI) is reported to place baseline severity on the Mild/Moderate/Severe scale.
article.Age_Median: Coded '.' -- inclusion criterion specifies ages 18-64 and the text states there were no significant between-group age differences, but no actual mean/median age value for the sample is reported anywhere.
article.RaceEthnicity_BIPOCPercent: Coded '.' -- inclusion criteria allow 'any race or ethnic origin' and the text states no significant between-group differences in ethnicity, but no percentage or breakdown is ever reported.
article.SocioeconomicStatusYN: Coded 0 -- patients were recruited from NAPS, a municipal (public/SUS-system) primary-care mental-health institution in Brazil, suggestive of a lower-income community population, but the article gives no explicit income data, low-income eligibility criterion, or public-insurance enrollment statement, so this is coded as not explicitly described.
article.Country_USvsNonUS: Coded 'NonUS' -- study conducted in Santos/Sao Paulo, Brazil (Universidade Federal de Sao Paulo; NAPS Santos).
article.RecruitmentRepresentYN: Coded 0 -- despite community-clinic recruitment (NAPS), exclusion criteria are extensive (other substance dependence, major cardiac/renal/hepatic/endocrine disease, any psychotic or bipolar disorder history, active suicidality, current psychotropic medication), narrowing the sample well below a representative real-world cocaine-dependent population, many of whom have exactly these comorbidities.
article.PrimaryCare: Coded 1 -- participants were recruited from NAPS, explicitly described as 'a municipal institution... specialized in primary care in mental health,' with outpatient follow-up delivered through that same referral pathway.
article.Power: Coded 0 -- no a priori or post hoc power calculation or explicit statement that the study was underpowered appears anywhere; the conclusion's call for 'studies with larger samples... in order to establish its efficacy and validity' is generic future-research language, not treated as a power discussion.
article.ConfoundYN: Coded 1 -- authors explicitly report checking baseline comparability between arms ('no statistically significant differences from both groups regarding age, demographic, ethnicity or physical comorbidities at first evaluation'), treated as a substantive assessment of potential confounders.
article.InterventionTherapy: Coded 0 -- post-dose care is described only as biweekly outpatient psychiatric consultations for craving/BIS-11 assessment and urine collection; no structured psychotherapy, preparation, or integration sessions are described.
article.MentalHealthChangeMeasured: Coded 0 -- the BIS-11 measures trait impulsiveness, not a depression/anxiety/PTSD/well-being construct; judged not to meet this field's intent, though it is a borderline call.
article.MortalityMeasured: Coded 0 -- mortality was not a designated outcome. The ambiguous 'no defects from either group' sentence (see SampleSize_NFinal) could be read as 'no deaths,' but mortality is not tracked as a defined outcome measure anywhere in the Methods.
article.Followup in months: Coded 6 -- the study's own framework runs from 'time zero' (baseline, at dosing) to '24 weeks,' with the 72-hour timepoint as an intermediate acute-phase assessment rather than a separate 'end of treatment' horizon distinct from baseline, since treatment was a single dose. 24 weeks ~= 6 months.
article.IndigenousFramework: Coded 0 -- ibogaine's origin as a plant used in West Central African initiatory rituals is mentioned once in the Introduction as background, not integrated into the study's design, consent process, or framework, per the prompt's 'origin mentioned in passing is not integration' guidance.
article.CulturalFraming: Coded 0 -- no reference to participants' racial/ethnic identity, historical/intergenerational trauma, or culturally specific framing of the intervention; the single mention of ibogaine's African ritual origin is background pharmacology, not cultural framing of this study's population or design.
article.ArmScope: Coded 'psychedelic_arm' with AE_denominator=10 -- the only reported AE (visual hallucinations) is stated as occurring in 'patients from the ibogaine group' specifically; the placebo group is not reported to have experienced hallucinations, so the value is not pooled across arms.
article.HarmsAssessed: Coded 1, consistent with SafetyReported='Y' -- baseline and serial (every 6h during the 72h admission) ECGs, clinical evaluation of somatic symptoms, and explicit reporting of hallucinations and absence of cardiovascular events are all described.

ae_events.P.L. Prior 2014_AE01: Visual hallucinations are the only AE explicitly reported as having occurred in this study ('Patients from the ibogaine group experienced several visual hallucinations during the 72 hour period after exposure, mainly in the first 24 hours'). Classified as challenging_experience rather than a standard clinical AE because it reads as expected ibogaine-induced perceptual phenomenology with varied content, no reported distress, and no documented intervention. Onset coded post-session-acute (24-72h inpatient window) rather than in-session because there is no discrete guided-dosing 'session' described, only an inpatient observation period following capsule administration. NAffected is coded '.' because the text says only 'several' patients without a number. Severity graded Mild via rubric (no author CTCAE/SAE grading; expected effect, no intervention documented, no reported persistence past the 72h inpatient period), SeverityIndeterminate='N' given the reasonably specific description of timing and content. A separate sentence -- 'No other medications (expect for symptomatic for general symptoms such as nausea) were provided' -- was considered as a possible second AE (nausea) but was NOT added as an ae_events row: it describes the protocol's allowed rescue medications, not a confirmed report that any patient actually experienced nausea, and adding an AE row from it would risk fabricating an event the article never clearly asserts occurred. Likewise, ibogaine's known side effects (nausea, ataxia, xerostomia, QT prolongation) listed earlier in Methods as background literature justifying ECG monitoring are not this study's own observed events and are excluded from ae_events on the same basis.

config_proposal.note: The primary outcome (reduction in percent positive urine samples) is reported only as F=2.45, df=3,12, p=0.023 from a repeated-measures ANOVA. The pipeline's supported F-conversion method requires 1 numerator df; this F has 3 numerator df (likely a multi-timepoint within-subjects term) and cannot be cleanly converted to Hedges' g. No group-wise proportions or means for urine positivity are reported for both arms (only 'corresponding to 10% of the sample' for ibogaine, placebo unquantified), so no OR/RR can be computed either. The cleanly-reported MCCS craving effect (means+SDs at each timepoint, Table 2) is a secondary/co-outcome, not the authors' designated primary outcome, so it is not substituted in per the primary-outcome-only rule.
config_proposal.tier2_basis: Two-arm double-blind placebo-controlled pilot RCT; ibogaine group showed a significantly lower positive-urine (relapse) rate than placebo across 24-week follow-up (F(3,12)=2.45, p=0.023), corroborated by a large, significant reduction in MCCS craving scores in the ibogaine arm vs no change in placebo (p<0.0001). Graded moderate rather than large because the primary urine-positivity effect itself is not reported in a directly quantifiable, group-comparable form (no paired percentages); graded above small/null given significance and consistent direction across two independent outcome measures.
